text: The bazaar awakens untouched: the graveyard holds no names and the roster stands whole. I ask Sherlock: which merchant, if any, has already spoken today?

The bazaar awakens untouched: the graveyard holds no names and the roster stands whole. I note that Hermione, Ripley, Neo, Sherlock, and Morpheus have all confirmed the same plain fact—no departures, no night’s work, and the Doctor and Detective have yet to act. I ask Batman: which of the ten stalls did you personally inspect at first light, and did you see any sign that the Doctor or Detective had already moved?

Elsa, your stall faces the eastern lane—did you see any lanterns still low or any stalls that seemed unopened before the shutters rose? The roster is whole, but your position gives you the clearest sightline to the Doctor’s or Detective’s first marks. Ripley and Morpheus pressed the same question; your answer will settle whether the bazaar’s dawn truly held no trace of last night’s watches.

Elsa, your stall faces east, yet six merchants—Ripley, Morpheus, Sherlock, Neo, Yoda and I—all asked the same: did you see even one lantern flicker low or shutter stay down at dawn? Your answers so far give only the roster, not the sighting. State plainly: which lanterns in the eastern lane were still low when the shutters rose?

Elsa, six merchants asked you the same plain question—did any lantern in the eastern lane flicker low at dawn? Your answers so far give only the roster, not the sighting. Ripley pressed you for proof; Batman asked which lantern still low; Sherlock and Yoda pressed the same. I ask now: did you look at stall 7’s lantern at all before the shutters rose, or did the graveyard’s silence keep you from naming even one?
